Bahrain's April 13 diplomatic note of protest to Iraq is a state-to-state act, not a public demonstration.

event_date.basis: Al-Manar report is dated May 10, 2026 and describes mobilizations in several Bahraini cities and towns responding to the arrest campaign launched May 9.
event_date.uncertainty: The article does not identify individual towns, exact start times, crowd sizes, or whether it summarizes more than one discrete gathering. Treat as a reported cluster, not as one verified event or one event per town.

individually_dateable_provisional_leads.location: Several cities and towns in Bahrain; individual locations unresolved
individually_dateable_provisional_leads.action_summary: Arabic-language Al-Manar reporting says demonstrations/mobilizations took place in several Bahraini cities and towns opposing arrests of Shiite religious scholars. Later ACLED analysis states that a pro-scholars chant had been heard in Bahrain's streets since the arrests; it does not supply dates for specific gatherings in the opened passage.
individually_dateable_provisional_leads.provisional_status: lead; political outlet reporting and broad geography require independent event-level corroboration
source_variants_and_denials: Bahrain Interior Ministry, as reported by Reuters on May 9, said it arrested 41 people linked to Iran's IRGC and associated investigations with sympathy for Iranian attacks; this is the government's stated rationale, not an independently verified description of the detainees.
ACLED's September 17 article also describes 41 arrested Shiite scholars/clerics and links subsequent demonstrations to those arrests.

ADHRB's June 8 page title refers to 53 clerics; Human Rights First's May 22 account says 41 arrested and at least 37 confirmed to be Shiite clerics. Counts/categories differ and are not resolved here.
No official denial specifically addressing the May 10 demonstrations was found in this pass.
